kultivator.screen.help.kapal_terbang: Three classes: Cloud Skiff (2 seats, Golden Core, 12 blocks/s, hull 200), Sect Ship (8 seats, Nascent Soul and a level-3 sect hall, 16 blocks/s, hull 400) and Sky Ark (12 seats, Deity Transformation and a level-7 hall, 20 blocks/s, hull 800). Craft the keel, use it on open ground, then right-click to board; the stern seat is the helm. The captain (owner or a sect mate): forward/back set the speed, left/right steer, jump climbs, sprint descends; sneak leaves the seat. The inventory key while seated, or sneak + right-click on the deck, opens the Helm: a 9-slot hold, repairs (8 planks + 1 Mid Spirit Stone per quarter of the hull), banner colour, Stow, and Sail to the sect hall, a map waypoint or another route. Fuel comes from the hold: Low stone 60 s, Mid 10 min, High 2 h, Supreme 24 h, Spirit Meteor Stone 4 min, Immortal Origin Stone 6 h in the Immortal Realm. Voyages over 1 500 blocks make a 512-block Cloud Leap every 30 s (fuel ×1.5); beyond 2 000 blocks there is a 15% chance of Sky Pirates. A docked ship (low and still for 2 s) puts out a deck you can walk on; FOLLOW disciples fly along and land when it docks. At the Helm the owner names the ship (shown above the masts) and picks a hull livery: Black Timber and Sea Jade are always open, Red Lacquer with a level-3 sect hall, White Cloud after driving off sky pirates, Golden Bamboo after a voyage of more than 3 000 blocks. Spirit weather under the keel changes the formation: thin mist fuel ×0.85, dense mist ×0.7 but speed ×0.85, purple dawn ×0.6 and speed ×1.1. A blood eclipse doubles the sky pirates' chance (at most 60%), twin moons make a Cloud Leap cost ×0.75 fuel, and a meteor shower may drop a Spirit Meteor Stone into the cloud net. Sky pirates come in a black raider that draws alongside; the band leaps down once the ship is low. Drive them off (no foe for 10 s) for spirit stones by their tier, sometimes a Pointer Scroll or a Spirit Meteor Stone. Ships never touch a block. Source: RMJ: Immortal Realm ch. 567; Zhang Hua's Bowuzhi.
